es: Usar con precisión el vocabulario de un pitch de negocio (scope, stake, leverage, margin, overheads, niche, viable, scale up) apoyado en cifras o razones.

vocabulary.es: viable, que funciona en la práctica
cobrar impulso, empezar a tener aceptación

teaching.en: The scope of the first phase is limited to one neighbourhood, which keeps overheads low while the owners test the idea.
teaching.es: El alcance de la primera fase se limita a un barrio, lo que mantiene bajos los gastos fijos mientras los dueños ponen a prueba la idea.
teaching.explanationEs: Scope es hasta dónde llega el proyecto; overheads son los gastos fijos: alquiler, electricidad, seguro.
segments: The scope of the first phase is limited to one neighbourhood,
which keeps overheads low while the owners test the idea.
teaching.audioText: The scope of the first phase is limited to one neighbourhood, which keeps overheads low while the owners test the idea.

teaching.en: Sara holds a twenty per cent stake in the workshop, so she shares both its profits and its losses.
teaching.es: Sara tiene una participación del veinte por ciento en el taller, así que comparte tanto sus beneficios como sus pérdidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Stake es la parte de un negocio que posee alguien; se usa con hold o have.
segments: Sara holds a twenty per cent stake in the workshop,
so she shares both its profits and its losses.
teaching.audioText: Sara holds a twenty per cent stake in the workshop, so she shares both its profits and its losses.

teaching.en: We can leverage Leo's contacts to break into a niche that the larger firms have overlooked.
teaching.es: Podemos aprovechar los contactos de Leo para abrirnos paso en un nicho que las empresas grandes han pasado por alto.
teaching.explanationEs: Leverage es un verbo transitivo (sin of); break into = entrar en un mercado difícil; niche = grupo pequeño y concreto.
segments: We can leverage Leo's contacts to break into
a niche that the larger firms have overlooked.
teaching.audioText: We can leverage Leo's contacts to break into a niche that the larger firms have overlooked.

teaching.en: With a margin of forty per cent on each repair, the workshop can gain traction even in a slow season.
teaching.es: Con un margen del cuarenta por ciento en cada reparación, el taller puede cobrar impulso incluso en una temporada floja.
teaching.explanationEs: Margin es la diferencia entre precio y coste; gain traction describe una idea que empieza a funcionar.
segments: With a margin of forty per cent on each repair,
the workshop can gain traction even in a slow season.
teaching.audioText: With a margin of forty per cent on each repair, the workshop can gain traction even in a slow season.

teaching.en: Once the pilot proves viable, we will scale up and benefit from economies of scale in buying parts.
teaching.es: Cuando el piloto demuestre ser viable, ampliaremos el negocio y nos beneficiaremos de las economías de escala al comprar piezas.
teaching.explanationEs: Viable significa que funciona en la práctica; scale up = ampliar; economies of scale = costes más bajos al crecer.
segments: Once the pilot proves viable, we will scale up
and benefit from economies of scale in buying parts.
teaching.audioText: Once the pilot proves viable, we will scale up and benefit from economies of scale in buying parts.

teaching.en: Winning a foothold in a crowded market is realistic only if the niche is clearly defined and the plan is viable.
teaching.es: Conseguir un punto de apoyo en un mercado saturado solo es realista si el nicho está bien definido y el plan es viable.
teaching.explanationEs: A foothold in es el primer apoyo firme en un mercado; se dice a foothold in, no on.
segments: Winning a foothold in a crowded market is realistic only if
the niche is clearly defined and the plan is viable.
teaching.audioText: Winning a foothold in a crowded market is realistic only if the niche is clearly defined and the plan is viable.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por ahora, el alcance del proyecto es deliberadamente pequeño.»

feedback.es: Scope es el alcance del proyecto: aquí, un solo barrio.

hint.es: Sustantivo para «hasta dónde llega el proyecto».

origin.text: We will start in a single neighbourhood and open a second workshop only when the first one makes a profit. For now, the ___ of the project is small on purpose.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del pitch usa el término con precisión?

choices.text: We plan to scope Leo's contacts in the cycling clubs to reach our first customers.
We plan to leverage Leo's contacts in the cycling clubs to reach our first customers.
We plan to stake Leo's contacts in the cycling clubs to reach our first customers.

feedback.es: Leverage es el verbo para sacar partido de algo que ya se tiene, como contactos; scope y stake son sustantivos.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que significa aprovechar lo que ya tienes.

origin.text: Leo has worked for ten years with the city's cycling clubs, and most of their members do not yet know that our workshop exists.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sara tiene una participación del treinta por ciento en el taller.»

answer.text: Sara holds a thirty per cent stake in the workshop

feedback.es: Holds a thirty per cent stake expresa la parte del negocio que posee Sara.

hint.es: Hold va con a thirty per cent stake.

prompt.es: Elige el término exacto para cada frase del pitch.

feedback.es: Cada definición apunta a un término: alcance, margen, gastos fijos y nicho.

sentences: The business will only serve one neighbourhood in phase one, so the ___ is small.
Customers pay fifty dollars and the parts cost thirty, so the ___ is twenty dollars on each repair.
Rent, electricity and insurance are the ___ we pay every month, whether we repair one bike or fifty.
No large firm serves this small group of cyclists, so it is a ___ that we can fill.
origin.text: A possible partner has asked Leo to explain four terms in his pitch. Choose the exact word for each sentence: scope, margin, overheads or niche.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conclusión del pitch usa el término con precisión?

choices.text: On these figures the business has a large stake, because income is clearly higher than costs.
On these figures the business is a niche, because income is clearly higher than costs.
On these figures the business is viable, because income is clearly higher than costs.

feedback.es: Viable significa que el negocio funciona en la práctica; que los ingresos superen los costes lo demuestra.

origin.text: Income next year is forecast at ninety thousand dollars, and all costs together come to sixty thousand.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué plan expone la hablante y en qué condiciones.

choices.text: To open a second branch only after the first one steadily makes a profit.
To open a second branch at once, since repeat customers already pay the costs.
To sell shares in the workshop once repeat customers bring a third of the income.

feedback.es: Ampliarán cuando el taller dé beneficios de forma estable, no antes; hasta entonces mantienen el mismo equipo.

origin.audio: The pilot has been running for six months and it has started to gain traction: repeat customers now account for a third of our income. Once the workshop steadily makes a profit, we will scale up and open a second branch, although we will keep the same small team until then.

prompt.es: Elige el término que completa cada frase del pitch.

feedback.es: Participación, aprovechar, ampliar y viable: cada espacio pide el término más preciso del pitch.

sentences: Mia owns thirty per cent of the company, so she has a big ___ in its success.
We will use our good name to win customers: we will ___ our good name.
The pilot worked, so we can now ___ up to three cities.
The figures show that we can earn money: the plan is ___.
origin.text: Pitch to a possible partner: Mia joined the project last year and now owns a share of the company. The pilot branch has covered its costs since May, and the first customers keep coming back. Leo believes that the idea is ready to grow.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué aconseja el inversor.

choices.text: Grow soon, since a fair margin and a sound idea already prove that the niche is real.
Wait to grow until regular customers show that the niche is real.
Accept his investment for a stake now and use the money to grow faster.

feedback.es: Aconseja no ampliar todavía: primero comprobar el nicho con clientes habituales y, si cobra impulso, volver a hablar de la participación; tener buen margen no sustituye esa prueba.

origin.audio: Your overheads are still high, so I would not advise you to scale up yet. First, test whether the niche is really there, and use your contacts to sign two or three regular customers. If the idea starts to gain traction, come back to us, and we will talk about a stake. I have seen many small firms grow too fast and lose the customers who made them successful. You have a sound idea and a fair margin, so there is no need to hurry. Let the numbers show that you can cover your overheads for six months, and the rest will follow.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad del negocio describe este fragmento?

choices.text: A narrow scope, caused by too few partners.
A thin margin, made worse by heavy overheads.
A weak stake, caused by too many partners.
A crowded niche, caused by strong competitors.

feedback.es: Cada venta deja casi nada tras pagar materiales y mano de obra, y el alquiler y los seguros se comen el resto: margen escaso y gastos fijos altos.

origin.text: The firm sells an excellent product, but each sale leaves almost nothing once the cost of materials and work has been paid. Whatever it earns is swallowed by rent, insurance and electricity.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase de pitch: margen, gastos fijos, viabilidad y crecimiento posterior.

answer.text: With a forty per cent margin and low overheads, the plan is viable, and once it gains traction we will scale up.
accepted: With a forty per cent margin and low overheads, the plan is viable, and once it gains traction we will scale up.
The margin is forty per cent and the overheads are low, so the business is viable and we will scale up later.
With a margin of forty per cent and overheads that are low, the idea is viable, and we will scale up when we are ready.

feedback.es: Una buena frase de pitch une cifra y término: margen, gastos fijos, viabilidad y ampliación posterior.

origin.text: Datos: margen del 40 % en cada reparación, gastos fijos bajos gracias a un alquiler económico y un piloto que ya tiene clientes habituales. Escribe una sola frase que exprese viabilidad y un plan de crecimiento posterior.

evidenceGroups: margin of forty per cent on

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra el inversor ante la idea de ampliar el negocio?

choices.text: Enthusiastic, and ready to back the expansion at once if the owners cut their overheads.
Doubtful about the niche itself, and not ready to discuss the plan any further.
Interested, but not ready to back expansion until one workshop proves itself.
Sceptical about the owners, whom he suspects of hiding how high their overheads are.

feedback.es: Le gusta la idea y cree en el nicho, pero quiere ver seis meses de un taller rentable antes de respaldar la ampliación.

origin.text: I like the idea, and I believe the niche is real. What worries me is the order of events: you plan to scale up before you have shown that a single workshop can cover its overheads. Show me six months in which it does, and my doubts will largely disappear.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Podemos aprovechar nuestro buen nombre para llegar a nuevos clientes.»

answer.text: We can leverage our good name to reach new customers

feedback.es: Leverage lleva complemento directo, sin of, y to reach expresa la finalidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «La idea aún no ha cobrado impulso fuera del barrio.»

feedback.es: Gain traction es la colocación habitual para una idea que empieza a tener aceptación.

origin.text: The idea is promising, yet it has not managed to ___ traction among customers outside the neighbourhood.
